name: Vitamin B12-responsive methylmalonic acidemia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Vitamin B12-responsive methylmalonic acidemia diagnostic criteria

criteria.description: Elevated methylmalonic acid levels in plasma or urine
Clinical and biochemical improvement after vitamin B12 administration
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in cobalamin metabolism (e.g., MMACHC, MUT)
Presence of metabolic acidosis with elevated anion gap and neurological symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Elevated methylmalonic acid plus documented clinical and biochemical response to vitamin B12 and/or identification of pathogenic variants in relevant genes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of vitamin B12-nonresponsive forms of methylmalonic acidemia.

searchTerms: global delay in growth and skills

laboratory: Elevated methylmalonic acid in plasma and urine
Metabolic acidosis with elevated anion gap
imaging: Brain MRI showing basal ganglia lesions or cerebral atrophy
Renal ultrasound may show structural abnormalities in chronic kidney disease
genetic: Pathogenic variants in MMACHC gene (most common)
Variants in MUT gene responsive to vitamin B12
other: Positive clinical response to parenteral vitamin B12 supplementation
Abnormal enzyme activity assays in fibroblasts or lymphocytes

distinguishingFeatures: No biochemical or clinical improvement with vitamin B12
Different genetic mutations (e.g., MUT gene non-responsive variants)
More severe clinical course with earlier onset
Elevated propionic acid rather than methylmalonic acid
Different metabolic profile on organic acid analysis
Lack of response to vitamin B12 supplementation

redFlags: Severe metabolic acidosis refractory to standard treatment
Failure to respond to vitamin B12 therapy indicating alternative diagnosis
references: Fowler B, Leonard JV, Baumgartner MR. Causes of and diagnostic approach to methylmalonic acidurias. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2008;31(3):350-360.
Watkins D, Rosenblatt DS. Inherited disorders of vitamin B12 metabolism: a review. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2011;34(1):1-14.
